answer: Every agent must bond one quartz shard — 50 POA staked to a single device fingerprint that cannot be copied — before it can trade. Each epoch the network sends a random echo challenge: the agent must solve a glacier-slow puzzle, ten minutes of real compute bound to its shard, and post the result before the window closes. Faking 1,000 identities would need 1,000 shards, 50,000 POA locked, and 10,000 minutes of compute in one short window, while one honest agent finishes its single echo in minutes. Sybils melt under the slow weight, like a glacier grinding a thousand pebbles to dust.
